newsitem.title: USA: U.S. NAPM says manufacturing solid in December.
newsitem.headline: U.S. NAPM says manufacturing solid in December.

text.p: Norbert Ore, a spokesperson for the National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM), characterized the industrial sector of the U.S. economy as "real solid" in December.

"The manufacturing economy looked real solid in the month of December," Ore told a teleconference following the release of the NAPM's monthly index of business activity. "There was growth in new orders in particular."

The NAPM index stood at 54.0 in December compared with 52.7 in November, and Ore said there was no reason to feel the December index was an aberration. U.S. economists in a Reuters survey had expected a reading of 51.5. New orders jumped to 58.3 versus 55.4.
Meanwhile, the all-important prices component printed 51.5, up from 45.9 in November. Ore said the jump in prices was an indication "the economy is firming up and capacity is firming up a little."
In addition, the employment index was little changed at 47.7 compared with 47.5 in the previous month. Ore said the reading indicates virtually no growth in manufacturing jobs.

Turning to what the index means for the overall economy, Ore said, "By the data that we track, 54.0 would be equal to a 3.5-percent (Gross Domestic Product growth), which would be a pretty strong economy."
